commenti.body: Reminds me of the end of the film with Patricia Arquette just thinking that there would've been more to her life than what she ended up with. Love how both filmmakers try to make sense of time and our lives.

Makes sense. I get the connection to Boyhood in terms of production, but I also interpret it as an endorsement of film as a medium which is special because of the power of editing.

Boyhood’s relationship to its own edit and process is also super fascinating to me beyond the “gimmick”, because in some ways it also seems like it’s in direct contrast to the philosophy of the film.
Good point. This view is probably applicable for film as a medium in general, but it’s something about the structure of Boyhood that makes Tarkovsky’s view so visible

No I completely agree, in case that wasn’t clear. I find Boyhood to be perplexing with how it plays with form like that (or rather doesn’t), but knowing the quote puts that into perspective a little bit. 

Also from Sculpting in Time, this is relavant imo

> But the virtue of cinema is that it appropriates time, complete with that material reality to which it is indissolubly bound, and which surrounds us day by day and hour by hour.
